_meta.description: Sparse BRSR -> GRESB overlay, keyed by framework_mappings.json brsr_id. Maps a BRSR disclosure to the GRESB Component and Aspect that asks for the same underlying data.
_meta.granularity: Component and Aspect, NOT indicator codes. Aspects are the stable, published vocabulary of the GRESB Standards; individual indicator codes are revised each Assessment year, so pinning them would rot and would risk citing a code that no longer exists.
_meta.assessments: GRESB runs two separate Assessments with DIFFERENT aspect vocabularies, so each row carries them separately. A row may map to one and not the other, which is a real difference and not an omission - e.g. Air Pollution and Biodiversity & Habitat exist only in Infrastructure, and Tenants & Community only in Real Estate.
_meta.real_estate_structure: Three Components. Management: 35 indicators across 5 Aspects (Leadership, Policies, ESG Reporting, Risk Management, Employee Engagement). Performance: 10 Aspects (Reporting Characteristics, Risk Assessment, Targets, Tenants & Community, Energy, GHG, Water, Waste, Data Monitoring & Review, Building Certifications). Development: measures sustainability in design, construction and renovation.
_meta.infrastructure_structure: Infrastructure Asset Assessment. Management: 24 indicators across 6 Aspects (Leadership, Policies, Targets, Reporting, Risk Management, Stakeholder Engagement). Performance: 12 Aspects (Implementation, Output & Impact, Health & Safety, Energy, Greenhouse Gas Emissions, Air Pollution, Water, Waste, Biodiversity & Habitat, Employees, Customers, Certifications & Awards).
_meta.applicability_warning: GRESB assesses REAL ESTATE AND INFRASTRUCTURE entities and funds. It is not a general-purpose corporate ESG benchmark. Most BRSR filers - a textile exporter, a pharmaceutical manufacturer, an IT services firm - do not participate in GRESB at all. This overlay is only meaningful for a real-estate or infrastructure client, and the UI must say so.
_meta.status: Indicative crosswalk for orienting work, NOT a certified equivalence and not a GRESB submission aid. GRESB collects asset-level data on its own templates with its own boundaries and reporting period rules; a BRSR figure is entity-level. Confirm every mapping against the current Assessment year's Reference Guide before relying on it.
_meta.invents_no_vocabulary: Every component and aspect name below is drawn verbatim from the published GRESB Assessment structure cited in sources. Nothing is coined here. gresb-mappings.test.ts asserts this against an allowlist.
_meta.deliberate_gaps: BRSR Principles 2, 5, 7 and 8 are mapped NOWHERE, on purpose. GRESB has no product-lifecycle aspect (P2), no human-rights aspect (P5), no policy-advocacy aspect (P7) and no statutory-CSR aspect (P8). Within P6, the India-specific disclosures (PAT scheme, Zero Liquid Discharge), environmental penalties, single-use plastic and internal carbon pricing have no GRESB counterpart and carry no mapping. 40 of the 77 crosswalk rows are mapped.
sources: GRESB Real Estate Assessment Reference Guide (current and prior years), https://documents.gresb.com/generated_files/real_estate/2025/real_estate/reference_guide/complete.html
GRESB Infrastructure Asset Assessment Reference Guide, https://documents.gresb.com/generated_files/infrastructure/2025/asset/reference_guide/complete.html
GRESB Infrastructure Fund Assessment Reference Guide, https://documents.gresb.com/generated_files/infrastructure/2025/fund/reference_guide/complete.html
GRESB, What is the GRESB Real Estate Assessment, https://www.gresb.com/faq/what-is-the-gresb-real-estate-assessment/

P1-G1.gresb_detail: Both Assessments open with oversight: who at board or equivalent level holds ESG accountability.

P1-G2.gresb_detail: A designated ESG committee or responsible body is the Leadership evidence in both Assessments.

P1-G4.gresb_detail: Anti-bribery and anti-corruption sits in the Policies aspect; GRESB asks for coverage, not just existence.

P1-G5.gresb_detail: Conflict-of-interest provisions are part of the governance policy set GRESB scores under Policies.

P1-G6.gresb_detail: Ethics awareness training for board, KMPs and employees is Employee Engagement evidence in Real Estate. Infrastructure has no equivalent Management aspect for internal ethics training.

P1-G7.gresb_detail: A grievance mechanism open to external stakeholders maps to Infrastructure's Stakeholder Engagement aspect. Real Estate's Management engagement aspect covers employees only, so no mapping there.

P1-G8.gresb_detail: The BRSR filing itself, plus any Annual or Sustainability Report, is what both Reporting aspects ask you to disclose. Note the aspects carry different names in the two Assessments.

P3-L1.gresb_detail: Headcount split by employment type and gender is Employees performance data in Infrastructure. Real Estate collects no equivalent workforce metric.

P3-L2.gresb_detail: Gender composition of the workforce and of management is reported under the Employees aspect.

P3-L7.gresb_detail: Occupational health and safety management system coverage is the core of the Health & Safety aspect.

P3-L8.gresb_detail: Recordable injuries and fatalities are the headline Health & Safety performance figures.

P3-L9.gresb_detail: Work-related ill health is reported alongside injury data under Health & Safety.

P3-L10.gresb_detail: Training hours evidence employee development: an engagement input in Real Estate's Management Component, a workforce metric in Infrastructure's Performance Component.

P3-L13.gresb_detail: Complaints raised on working conditions and safety, filed against resolved, support the Health & Safety aspect.

P4-Q1.gresb_detail: Identifying the stakeholder groups is the first Stakeholder Engagement question in Infrastructure.

P4-Q2.gresb_detail: Channels and frequency of engagement: Real Estate asks this about tenants and the surrounding community; Infrastructure asks it as a Management practice.

P4-Q3.gresb_detail: Material issues surfaced through engagement are the output Stakeholder Engagement asks you to evidence.

P6-E1.gresb_detail: Purchased electricity is the primary energy consumption input in both Assessments. GRESB wants it asset by asset, where BRSR reports it entity-wide.

P6-E2.gresb_detail: Fuel consumption completes the energy picture and is also the activity data behind Scope 1.

P6-E3.gresb_detail: Biomass and recovered waste heat are reported within the energy consumption breakdown.

P6-E4.gresb_detail: Total energy is the Energy aspect's headline figure. ⚠️ GRESB normalises by floor area or asset output, not by rupee of turnover, so the BRSR intensity does not transfer - only the absolute total does.

P6-E5.gresb_detail: Renewable share is part of the energy mix both Assessments collect.

P6-E7.gresb_detail: Withdrawal by source is the Water aspect's consumption input.

P6-E8.gresb_detail: Water consumption is the Water aspect's headline figure. The same intensity caveat as energy applies: GRESB normalises differently.

P6-E9.gresb_detail: Discharge by destination and treatment method is collected under Water.

P6-E11.gresb_detail: Scope 1 is reported directly. Note the aspect is named GHG in Real Estate and Greenhouse Gas Emissions in Infrastructure.

P6-E12.gresb_detail: Scope 2. ⚠️ GRESB asks for both location-based and market-based where available; BRSR asks for one figure, so check which basis your number uses.

P6-E13.gresb_detail: Scope 3. Voluntary as a BRSR Leadership indicator, and reported by category in GRESB.

P6-E14.gresb_detail: Emission intensity. Same normalisation caveat: the BRSR per-rupee basis is not the GRESB basis.

P6-E15.gresb_detail: Reduction targets and progress against them. ⚠️ Targets sits in the Performance Component in Real Estate but in the Management Component in Infrastructure.

P6-E16.gresb_detail: Offsets purchased or retired are disclosed alongside gross emissions, never netted into them.

P6-E17.gresb_detail: Total waste generated, split hazardous and non-hazardous, is the Waste aspect's input.

P6-E18.gresb_detail: Waste diverted from disposal - reused, recycled, other recovery - is the diversion rate GRESB scores.

P6-E19.gresb_detail: Waste directed to disposal by method completes the Waste aspect.

P6-E20.gresb_detail: NOx, SOx and particulate matter map to Infrastructure's Air Pollution aspect. Real Estate has no air-pollution aspect, so there is no mapping there.

P6-E22.gresb_detail: Operations in or adjacent to ecologically sensitive areas map to Biodiversity & Habitat, which exists only in the Infrastructure Assessment.

P6-E25.gresb_detail: Climate-related risks and opportunities. ⚠️ Real Estate assesses this as Performance Risk Assessment; Infrastructure as Management Risk Management.

P6-E26.gresb_detail: Scenario analysis for climate resilience is the deepest part of both risk aspects.

P9-C1.gresb_detail: Complaints received and resolved: tenants and community in Real Estate, customers in Infrastructure.

P9-C6.gresb_detail: Satisfaction surveys and their outcomes are collected by both aspects.
